items.title: The Sweet Trap
items.question: Human brains reward sugar and fat intensely — perfect for scarce savannas, catastrophic for supermarket aisles. What makes these cravings mismatched today?
choices: Cravings evolved for scarcity, not abundance
items.correctAnswer: Cravings evolved for scarcity, not abundance
items.correctExplanation: Cravings evolved for scarcity — rare energy bonanzas deserved celebration; constant bonanzas deserve restraint the wiring lacks. Stone-age rules, all-you-can-eat world.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is cravings evolved for scarcity, not abundance. Engineers exploit wiring they didn't create: prehistoric sugar existed (honey, fruit) but rarely. Abundance, not novelty, breaks the system.
items.lessonContent:
Wiring built for scarcity misfires in abundance.
Celebrate-rare-energy rules corrupt under constant supply.
Exploiters didn't create the vulnerabilities.
Abundance breaks more systems than novelty does.
Share this: spot one scarcity-craving misfiring.

items.title: The Salt Legacy
items.question: Humans crave salt fiercely though excess drives hypertension. In ancestral environments, salt was vanishingly rare. What does the craving record?
items.correctExplanation: Ancient scarcity — appetites formed where salt was precious now operate where shakers overflow. The craving is a fossil, not a prescription.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is ancient scarcity written into appetite. Kidneys handle salt fine at ancestral doses; modern loads exceed design specs. Fossil appetites mislead in changed worlds.
items.lessonContent:
Appetites fossilize past scarcities faithfully.
Fossils mislead when worlds change fast.
Design specs assume ancestral doses.
Cravings record history, never prescriptions.
Share this: taste one fossil appetite knowingly.

items.title: The Snake Alarm
items.question: People fear snakes and spiders far more than cars and sockets, though the latter kill vastly more. Prepared learning explains the gap. What is primed?
choices: Fear of ancient threats over modern ones
items.correctAnswer: Fear of ancient threats over modern ones
items.correctExplanation: Ancient-threat priming — evolution pre-wired snake/spider fears; cars arrived too recently for wiring. Statistics lose to preparedness.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is fear of ancient threats over modern ones. Nobody calculates: prepared circuits fire at scales and legs while ignoring bumpers and volts. New killers lack old alarms.
items.lessonContent:
Prepared circuits fire at ancient shapes.
New killers lack old alarms entirely.
Statistics lose to wiring consistently.
Priming predates the automobile by eons.
Share this: fear one socket proportionally.

items.title: The Foraging Feed
items.question: Social feeds deliver unpredictable rewards — likes, replies, novelties — on variable schedules. Which ancient system does this hijack?
choices: The foraging system built for patchy food
items.correctAnswer: The foraging system built for patchy food
items.correctExplanation: Patchy-food foraging — variable-ratio rewards drove persistent searching; feeds farm the same circuit with information pellets. Slot machines and savannas share schedules.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the foraging system built for patchy food. Immune, balance, and thirst systems miss it: unpredictable pellets sustain checking exactly as berry bushes sustained ranging. Engineers farm ancient schedules.
items.lessonContent:
Variable rewards sustain checking endlessly.
Information pellets farm foraging circuits.
Slot schedules predate silicon by eons.
Patchy payoffs drive persistent ranging.
Share this: notice one foraging loop today.

items.title: The Status Scroll
items.question: Teen anxiety tracks social-media rank-checking: likes counted, followers compared, status perpetually audited. Which old machinery runs this?
choices: Hierarchy tracking built for small bands
items.correctAnswer: Hierarchy tracking built for small bands
items.correctExplanation: Small-band hierarchy tracking — status mattered intensely among 150 familiars; global leaderboards overload the gauge. Dunbar-scale minds meet planetary audiences.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is hierarchy tracking built for small bands. Eyes, thumbs, and math miss it: rank-monitoring evolved for tribes, and feeds scale the tribe to billions. Overload, not vanity, drives the anxiety.
items.lessonContent:
Tribal gauges break on planetary scales.
Rank-monitoring evolved for 150 familiars.
Overload, not vanity, drives scroll anxiety.
Audiences outgrew the machinery badly.
Share this: audit one leaderboard's effect.

items.title: The Jersey War
items.question: Sports fandom, brand loyalty, and party rage share a psychology: instant us-versus-them, love for insiders, fury at outsiders. What ancient program runs?
items.correctExplanation: Tribal coalitional psychology — parochial altruism: sacrifice for us, suspicion of them. Jerseys and ballots press Stone-Age buttons.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is tribal coalitional psychology. Colors, training, and economics miss it: brains built for band competition sort modern life into teams effortlessly. Buttons pressed are Pleistocene originals.
items.lessonContent:
Band competition sorts modern life effortlessly.
Buttons pressed are Pleistocene originals.
Insiders loved, outsiders suspected: the default.
Jerseys channel ancient coalitions.
Share this: catch one tribal button pressed.

items.title: The Doom Scroll
items.question: Bad news grips attention while good news slides past — so feeds optimize for outrage and the world feels like it's burning. What bias powers the business model?
items.correctExplanation: Threat-monitoring negativity bias — attending to danger kept ancestors alive; platforms monetize the vigilance. Burning-world feelings are engagement metrics.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is negativity bias from threat monitoring. Literacy, rays, and positivity miss it: survival tuned attention to threats, and feeds farm that tuning. Outrage is inventory, not accident.
items.lessonContent:
Survival tuning becomes engagement inventory.
Threats grip; comforts slide past unnoticed.
Burning-world feelings are metrics, not news.
Vigilance monetized distorts perceived reality.
Share this: count one feed's threat ratio.

items.title: The Chair Sentence
items.question: Bodies built for varied daily movement now sit for ten-plus hours; metabolic and spinal complaints follow. What does the chair impose?
items.correctExplanation: Stillness on movement-designed machinery — joints, glucose handling, and spines expect ranging, not perching. Chairs aren't evil; unbroken sitting contradicts design.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is stillness on movement-designed machinery. Air, company, and uprightness miss it: metabolism idles when muscles do. Breaks, not furniture swaps, pay the movement debt.
items.lessonContent:
Metabolisms idle when muscles do.
Design expects ranging, never perching.
Debts accrue hourly; breaks repay.
Machinery mismatched malfunctions predictably.
Share this: break one sitting hour today.

items.title: The Midnight Sun
items.question: Screens bathe eyes in daylight-spectrum light past midnight, suppressing melatonin and shifting sleep later. What signal gets scrambled?
items.correctExplanation: The light-dark code — brains read photons as time; midnight brightness reads as extended day. Melatonin obeys light, not clocks.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the circadian light-dark code. Hunger, bones, and blood miss it: photosensitive cells report 'daytime' to the master clock. Screens forge daylight after dark.
items.lessonContent:
Photons read as time by master clocks.
Midnight brightness forges false daytime.
Melatonin obeys light, never wall clocks.
Spectrums carry schedules silently.
Share this: dim one midnight screen.

items.title: The Shorted Night
items.question: Pre-industrial sleep studies suggest longer, broken slumbers; modern schedules compress rest into short single blocks with rising complaints. What changed most?
items.correctExplanation: Schedules compressing sleep — need stayed ~7-9 hours while electric evenings and early alarms squeeze both ends. Biology constant, timetable brutal.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is schedules compressing sleep below need. Genes, dreams, and pillows miss it: need didn't shrink, nights did. Complaints track the gap between biology and timetable exactly.
items.lessonContent:
Needs stayed; nights shrank around them.
Timetables brutalize constant biologies.
Complaints track need-timetable gaps.
Electric evenings squeeze both ends.
Share this: protect one sleep edge tonight.

items.title: The Drunken Monkey
items.question: Fruit-eating primates evolved strong alcohol tolerance, and humans kept both the enzymes and the attraction. What does this lineage explain?
items.correctExplanation: Fermented calories attracted — ripe fallen fruit announced itself by ethanol; attraction to the signal persists past its usefulness. Wild parties, outdated invitations.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is why fermented calories attract us. Speeches, willpower, and grapes miss it: ethanol marked ripe energy, and the marker outlived the orchard. Distilled spirits overdose an ancient cue.
items.lessonContent:
Markers outlive the orchards they marked.
Ethanol announced ripe energy reliably.
Distilled doses overdose ancient cues.
Attractions persist past usefulness.
Share this: smell one outdated invitation.

items.title: The Indoor Shortfall
items.question: Office life across temperate zones leaves widespread vitamin-D shortfalls, though skin manufactures it free from sunlight. What created the gap?
items.correctExplanation: Indoor living — skin factories idle without UV shifts. Shortfalls track hours inside, not latitude alone.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is indoor living blocking UV synthesis. Conspiracies, dimmer suns, and dairies miss it: factories need shifts, and office workers skip them. Step outside; the synthesis resumes.
items.lessonContent:
Skin factories idle without UV shifts.
Shortfalls track indoor hours precisely.
Free synthesis needs only exposure.
Modern roofs block ancient chemistry.
Share this: take one UV shift today.

items.title: The Schooled Eyes
items.question: East Asian myopia exploded from ~20% to ~90% within schooled generations — far too fast for genes. What protects children's eyesight?
items.correctExplanation: Outdoor daylight — bright light triggers retinal dopamine that slows eyeball elongation. Classrooms didn't change genes; they stole the sun.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is daily outdoor daylight hours. Glasses, carrots, and fonts miss it: eyes elongate without bright-light braking. Two hours outside outperforms every lens sold.
items.lessonContent:
Bright light brakes eyeball elongation.
Generational explosions rule out genes.
Classrooms stole what playgrounds gave.
Daylight doses protect developing eyes.
Share this: log two outdoor hours.

items.title: The Cheap Alarm
items.question: Anxiety feels excessive — yet false alarms cost little while missed threats kill. Nesse's smoke-detector principle says defenses are calibrated how?
items.correctExplanation: Cheap alarms over misses — defense systems accept a hundred false fires to catch one real blaze. Anxiety is smoke-detector logic, not malfunction.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is cheap alarms over costly misses. Calm, thrift, and silence miss it: asymmetric costs favor twitchy systems. Panic attacks are detectors doing exactly their cheap-alarm job.
items.lessonContent:
Asymmetric costs favor twitchy systems.
Hundred false fires buy one real catch.
Detectors do cheap-alarm jobs faithfully.
Anxiety is calibration, rarely malfunction.
Share this: thank one false alarm.

items.title: The Nausea Guard
items.question: Pregnancy nausea peaks exactly when embryos are most vulnerable to toxins, targeting bitter plants and meat. What does the sickness shield?
items.correctExplanation: The embryo — nausea as fetal bodyguard, rejecting exactly what harms development most. Misery with a protective assignment.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the embryo from dietary toxins. Comfort, bonding, and revenues miss it: timing plus targets reveal defense. Morning sickness guards mornings that matter.
items.lessonContent:
Timing plus targets reveal defenses.
Misery can carry protective assignments.
Bitter-and-meat aversions guard development.
Nausea bodyguards the vulnerable weeks.
Share this: respect one nausea signal.

items.title: The Narrow Gate
items.question: Human birth is uniquely perilous: big-brained infants must pass pelvises narrowed for upright walking. What evolutionary trade-off causes this?
items.correctExplanation: Brains versus bipedal pelvises — the obstetric dilemma: encephalization pushed up, locomotion pushed in. Birth pain is geometry, not failure.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is brains versus bipedal pelvises. Doctors, growth rates, and diets miss it: walking upright narrowed the gate that thinking widened. Peril is the compromise made flesh.
items.lessonContent:
Geometry, not failure, explains birth peril.
Encephalization pushed; locomotion constrained.
Compromises made flesh hurt by design.
Narrow gates plus big heads equal drama.
Share this: honor one narrow gate crossed.

items.title: The Grandmother Dividend
items.question: Human females live decades past fertility — nearly unique among primates. The grandmother hypothesis says post-reproductive years pay through what?
items.correctExplanation: Grandchildren surviving better — experienced alloparents raise grandoffspring survival enough to select for longevity itself. Menopause funds grandmothers.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is grandchildren surviving better. Aging, wealth, and appetite miss it: post-fertile help boosts descendants' fitness directly. Longevity evolved through grandchildren's eyes.
items.lessonContent:
Post-fertile help boosts descendant fitness.
Longevity evolved through grandchildren's survival.
Alloparents fund their own selection.
Menopause is strategy, never malfunction.
Share this: thank one grandmother dividend.

items.title: The Early Peanut
items.question: Avoiding peanuts increased childhood allergy rates; feeding peanuts early (LEAP trial) cut allergy ~80%. What builds the tolerance?
items.correctExplanation: Early oral exposure — the gut taught tolerance while avoidance taught alarm. Timing, not dose, decides allergy curricula.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is early oral exposure building tolerance. Bans and delays backfired: immune systems learn friend from food by meeting it early. Windows open, then close — feed accordingly.
items.lessonContent:
Windows open briefly, then close firmly.
Guts teach tolerance by early meeting.
Avoidance curricula graduate alarmists.
Timing decides allergy outcomes most.
Share this: feed windows, not fears.

items.title: The Loud Hours
items.question: Ears evolved for transient natural sounds, not hours of high-decibel streams. Chronic loud listening destroys first and irreversibly what?
items.correctExplanation: Inner-ear hair cells — mammalian cochleae don't regrow them. Transient design meets continuous assault; silence can't restore the dead.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is inner-ear hair cells. Skin, skull, and nose miss it: the transducers themselves die without replacement. Volume limits are design limits, not suggestions.
items.lessonContent:
Transducers die without replacement parts.
Design limits are not suggestions.
Continuous assaults break transient machinery.
Silence restores nothing dead.
Share this: lower one volume today.

items.title: The Snapping Gaze
items.question: Phones farm the orienting response — attention snapping to novelty, motion, and alerts. Brains built for savanna surprises now serve whom?
items.correctExplanation: The novelty-detection reflex — orienting to movement and pings once spotted predators; now it spots notifications. Savanna alarms ring for silicon.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the novelty-detection reflex. Knees, modes, and dives miss it: snap-to-novelty kept foragers alive and keeps users scrolling. Alerts are artificial predators of attention.
items.lessonContent:
Snap-to-novelty kept foragers alive.
Alerts are artificial attention predators.
Savanna alarms ring for silicon now.
Reflexes serve whoever triggers them.
Share this: starve one artificial predator.

items.title: The Blunt Index
items.question: BMI brands muscular athletes obese and frail lightweights healthy. As a health gauge, what does the index completely ignore?
items.correctExplanation: Body composition — mass over height-squared cannot see muscle versus fat. Blunt indices misclassify both tails.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is body composition entirely. Height, age, and timing miss it: the formula lacks any fat-versus-lean term. Populations average fine; individuals deserve better gauges.
items.lessonContent:
Formulas lacking terms misclassify tails.
Muscle and fat weigh identically here.
Population tools fail individual cases.
Composition, not mass, decides health.
Share this: retire one blunt index.

items.title: The Broken Clock
items.question: Night-shift workers carry higher metabolic and cancer risks; WHO flags circadian disruption as probably carcinogenic. What does chronic desync damage?
items.correctExplanation: Clock-coordinated physiology — hormones, repair, and cell cycles run on circadian timetables that shift work scrambles. Desync is systemic, not sleepiness.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is clock-coordinated physiology. Pay, calendars, and alarms miss it: bodies schedule repair and division by light-dark cycles. Scrambling timetables breaks more than mornings.
items.lessonContent:
Bodies schedule repairs by light cycles.
Scrambling timetables breaks systemically.
Desync exceeds mere sleepiness vastly.
Timetables are physiological, not social.
Share this: guard one circadian edge.

items.title: The Longer Day
items.question: Eastward flights (losing hours) punish travelers more than equal westward ones. The brain's internal day runs slightly longer than 24 hours. Why does this asymmetry matter?
choices: The brain's day runs slightly long
items.correctAnswer: The brain's day runs slightly long
items.correctExplanation: The internal day runs ~24.2 hours — delaying (westward) rides the natural drift; advancing (eastward) fights it. Direction matters because clocks have grain.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the brain's day runs slightly long. Food, politics, and luggage miss it: phase delays cooperate with biology while advances oppose it. Fly with the drift when possible.
items.lessonContent:
Internal days exceed 24 hours slightly.
Delays cooperate; advances oppose.
Direction matters because clocks have grain.
Fly with biological drift when possible.
Share this: delay, don't advance, once.

items.title: The Atomized Tribe
items.question: Tribal brains marooned in atomized cities report record loneliness with measurable cardiac and immune costs. What mismatch drives the epidemic?
items.correctExplanation: Band-sized needs in mass society — belonging systems built for dense kin networks starve among millions of strangers. Crowds don't cure tribal hunger.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is band-sized needs meeting mass society. Excess friends, empathy, and reunions miss it: contact without belonging starves the system. Density differs from community entirely.
items.lessonContent:
Contact without belonging starves systems.
Density differs from community entirely.
Crowds never cure tribal hunger.
Belonging needs bands, not masses.
Share this: band one stranger today.

items.title: The Exaggerated Lure
items.question: Tinbergen's birds preferred giant painted eggs over their own; junk food, feeds, and pornography exploit the same glitch. What defines a supernormal stimulus?
items.correctExplanation: Exaggeration beyond natural maxima — instincts calibrated to wild ranges misfire on amplified fakes. Bigger buttons press harder, truthfully or not.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is exaggeration beyond natural maxima. Naturalness, noise, and deprivation miss it: preferences evolved over real ranges get hijacked past their peaks. Calibration breaks past maxima.
items.lessonContent:
Calibrations break past natural maxima.
Bigger buttons press harder, truly or falsely.
Hijacked instincts misfire on fakes.
Wild ranges bound honest preferences.
Share this: spot one exaggerated lure.
